advances: The proposed single-coordinate no-loss invariant is false for the arbitrary finite cores allowed by the definitions in accepted `8668ed0d436b9cba`. An exact counterexample has spatial dimension r=2, cap T=32, beta=0, twelve exposed core sites, rational weights, and the legal convex four-site cost g=(0,1,2,3). Its actual ambient depths and both cap minima are calculated below. Replication at the same spatial dimension shows that replacing the floor 1/4 by any fixed positive floor does not repair the arbitrary-core assertion. The cores in this counterexample are not lattice-complete and their weights are not log-affine. This does not refute the version restricted to complete convex cores with log-affine weights, or the locked mixed-integer conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted `8668ed0d436b9cba` is used for the arbitrary-core model and notation, accepted `c5f6533ba1c11991` only for its unconditional scalar calibration (Cal1), and accepted `01a4100542206b94` only for its unconditional uniform complete-lattice-support cubic moment lower bound. Every counterexample depth and both exact cap minima are proved above.
proof:
First we establish exact branch isolation in the ambient spaces. For every site \(\mathbf v_i\), the affine functional \(\ell_i(\mathbf x)=2ix_1-x_2\) satisfies
\(\ell_i(\mathbf v_j)=i^2-(j-i)^2\). Thus \(\ell_i\) is uniquely maximized at \(\mathbf v_i\), with a gap at least one to every other spatial site.

Consider either the core or combined support, and write \(w=t\) or \(w=(y,t)\) for the remaining coordinates. A containing ambient closed halfspace restricts on the branch \(\mathbf x=\mathbf v_i\) to a closed halfspace in the \(w\)-space, or to the entire \(w\)-space. Consequently its mass is at least the minimum containing-halfspace mass of that branch, divided by the full original normalizer. Conversely, if a branch halfspace is \(K=\lbrace w:a\cdot w\ge b\rbrace\), the ambient halfspace
\(\lbrace(\mathbf x,w):M(\ell_i(\mathbf x)-i^2)+a\cdot w\ge b\rbrace\)
has exactly the same intersection with the branch and excludes every other branch for all sufficiently large positive \(M\). Such an \(M\) exists because the support is finite and the spatial gap is at least one. This proves equality with the normalized branch depth, rather than only a lower bound. In particular, if the branch has constant atom weight \(q_{\mathbf v_i}\), its actual depth is \(q_{\mathbf v_i}\) times its unweighted branch depth count, divided by the full normalizer. This argument includes every ambient normal and all closed-halfspace boundary atoms.

For \(0\le U<32\), only the \(4m\) low-energy branches are present. Write \(u_U\) for the uniform scalar law on \(\lbrace0,\ldots,U\rbrace\), and write \(v_U\) for the uniform planar law on
\(E_U=\lbrace(y,t)\in\mathbb Z^2:0\le y\le3,\ y\le t\le U\rbrace\). Exact branch isolation gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
8^3M_3(p_{\rm core}^{(U)})
&=\frac8{m^3}M_3(u_U),\\
8^4M_3(p_4^{(U)})
&=\frac{64}{m^3}M_3(v_U).
\end{aligned}
$$
Only the unconditional scalar calibration (Cal1), with exponent 3, of accepted `c5f6533ba1c11991` is used here: \(M_3(u_U)\ge1/32\). No arithmetic moment hypothesis from that fact is assumed. Also, \(E_U\) is precisely the lattice intersection of the compact convex set \(\lbrace(y,t):0\le y\le3,\ y\le t\le U\rbrace\). Hence the unconditional uniform complete-support estimate of accepted `01a4100542206b94`, in arithmetic ambient dimension 2 and exponent 3, gives \(M_3(v_U)\ge1/256\). Both estimates include lower-dimensional and singleton supports. It follows that every earlier core cap and every earlier combined cap has the corresponding normalized moment at least \(1/(4m^3)\).

At \(U=32\), each low core branch is the uniform height interval \(\lbrace0,\ldots,32\rbrace\), with depth count \(\min\lbrace t+1,33-t\rbrace\) at height \(t\). Each high core branch consists of one atom of weight 33 at height 32. Put
\(A=\sum_{t=0}^{32}\min\lbrace t+1,33-t\rbrace^3=41905\). The full core normalizer is \(Z_{\rm core}(32)=4m\cdot33+8m\cdot33=396m\), so exact branch isolation gives
$$
8^3M_3(p_{\rm core}^{(32)})
=512\frac{4m\cdot41905+8m\cdot33^4}{(396m)^4}
=\frac{19309976}{96059601m^3}
<\frac1{4m^3}.
$$
Together with the earlier-cap estimates, this already determines the core cap minimum exactly.

It remains to calculate every unweighted branch depth in \(E_{32}\). Write its unnormalized depth count as \(d(y,t)\). The complete depth table is specified by the following formulas; the last column gives the sum of the cubes along that entire column.

| Column | Heights | Exact depth count | Cubic sum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \(y=0\) | \(0\le t\le32\) | \(\min\lbrace t+1,33-t\rbrace\) | 41905 |
| \(y=1\) | \(1\le t\le32\) | \(3\min\lbrace t,33-t\rbrace-1\) | 920416 |
| \(y=2\) | \(2\le t\le32\) | \(\min\lbrace3t-4,98-3t,46\rbrace\) | 810106 |
| \(y=3\) | \(3\le t\le32\) | \(\min\lbrace t-2,33-t\rbrace\) | 28800 |

We prove this table against all planar closed halfspaces. A minimum can be sought among halfplanes whose boundary passes through the queried point and no other support point: translating a boundary to the root removes no required root, and then a sufficiently small generic perturbation preserves every strict sign, adds no previously excluded point, and keeps the root on the boundary. In particular we may take a nonvertical boundary with generic slope. Lower halfplanes through \((j,t)\) have the form \(u\le t+s(y-j)\). Their count in column \(y\) is
\(\operatorname{clip}(\lfloor t+s(y-j)\rfloor-y+1,0,33-y)\), where \(\operatorname{clip}(a,0,b)=\min\lbrace\max\lbrace a,0\rbrace,b\rbrace\).

The affine reflection \((y,t)\mapsto(y,32+y-t)\) preserves \(E_{32}\), swaps upper and lower halfplanes, and preserves all atom counts. Thus it is enough to compare lower-halfplane counts at a root and its reflection. For the two exterior columns, restriction to the root's column gives the scalar depth lower bound in the table. An arbitrarily steep slope can exclude all other columns while realizing either scalar ray, so those two bounds are exact.

For \(j=1\), the root column contributes \(t\) points. Before clipping, the counts in columns 0 and 2 sum to \(2t-1\), because genericity gives \(\lfloor t-s\rfloor+\lfloor t+s\rfloor=2t-1\). Their column lengths are 33 and 31. For two raw counts of nonnegative sum \(c\), clipping to column lengths \(L,R\) leaves a sum at least \(\min\lbrace c,L,R\rbrace\): if neither upper cutoff is used, lower clipping only increases the raw sum, and if an upper cutoff is used, that column alone contributes at least this minimum. Consequently every lower halfplane at \((1,t)\) has count at least \(t+\min\lbrace2t-1,31\rbrace\). For \(1\le t\le16\), this is \(3t-1\), attained by the slope \(s=(5-2t)/4\): column 3 is empty, and columns 0 and 2 have no clipping that changes their raw sum. The reflected root has height \(33-t\ge17\), whose lower-halfplane count is at least \((33-t)+31\ge48\). This proves the stated formula for the entire \(y=1\) column by reflection.

For \(j=2\), the root column contributes \(t-1\) points, and the raw counts in columns 1 and 3 sum to \(2t-3\). Their lengths are 32 and 30. The same clipping argument bounds every lower-halfplane count by at least \(t-1+\min\lbrace2t-3,30\rbrace\). For \(2\le t\le16\), the value \(3t-4\) is attained by \(s=(2t+1)/4\): column 0 is empty and columns 1 and 3 have no clipping that changes their raw sum. The reflected root has height \(34-t\ge18\), and its lower-halfplane count is at least \((34-t)+29\ge47\). At the central height \(t=17\), the lower bound is 46 and the slope \(s=33/2\) attains it by retaining exactly 16 points in column 2 and all 30 points in column 3. The reflection fixes this central root. This proves the entire \(y=2\) column and completes the actual-depth verification.

The four cubic sums in the table follow from integer summation. In particular, the interior-column sums are \(2\sum_{j=1}^{16}(3j-1)^3=920416\) and \(2\sum_{j=1}^{15}(3j-1)^3+46^3=810106\). Thus
\(\sum_{(y,t)\in E_{32}}d(y,t)^3=1801227\), and \(|E_{32}|=33+32+31+30=126\).

In the combined law at cap 32, each of the \(4m\) low branches is exactly \(E_{32}\), with atom weight one and the depth counts just proved. Each of the \(8m\) high branches contains only \((y,t)=(0,32)\), with weight and unnormalized branch depth 33. The full original normalizer is \(Z_4(32)=4m\cdot126+8m\cdot33=768m\). Hence
$$
8^4M_3(p_4^{(32)})
=4096\frac{4m\cdot1801227+8m\cdot33^4}{(768m)^4}
=\frac{1391023}{7077888m^3}
<\frac1{4m^3}.
$$
The earlier-cap estimates therefore establish the combined cap minimum exactly as well. No cap has been discarded, conditioned away, or replaced by a residual normalizer.

Finally, the strict comparison between the two exact minima is the integer inequality
\(1391023\cdot96059601=133621114361823<136673847410688=19309976\cdot7077888\). Its ratio is \(4948930161549/5061994348544<1\), independent of \(m\). The same exposed-site argument works for all \(12m\) parabola vertices at the same spatial dimension. Each normalizer is multiplied by \(m\), and each unnormalized cubic-depth numerator by \(m\), explaining the exact \(m^{-3}\) scaling. Choosing \(m\) as in the statement proves the assertion for every positive fixed floor. The missing lattice points and the failure of log-affine weights persist for every \(m\), so this replication does not extend the counterexample to the complete convex/log-affine class.
statement:
For every integer m>=1, set r=2, T=32, beta=0, and define the spatial core sites, energies, and weights by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf v_i&=(i,i^2),\qquad
D_{\rm core}=\lbrace\mathbf v_i:0\le i<12m\rbrace,\\
h_{\rm core}(\mathbf v_i)&=
\begin{cases}0,&0\le i<4m,\\32,&4m\le i<12m,\end{cases}
\qquad
q_{\mathbf v_i}=
\begin{cases}1,&0\le i<4m,\\33,&4m\le i<12m.\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$
The variable \(\mathbf x\) of accepted `8668ed0d436b9cba` takes values \(\mathbf v_i\) here; its \(r,T,\beta,h_{\rm core},q_{\mathbf x},U,p_{\rm core}^{(U)}\) retain their meanings. Explicitly, for every integer \(0\le U\le32\), the original core support is
\(A_{{\rm core},U}=\lbrace(\mathbf v_i,t):h_{\rm core}(\mathbf v_i)\le t\le U,\ t\in\mathbb Z\rbrace\), with unnormalized weight \(q_{\mathbf v_i}\) and normalizer \(Z_{\rm core}(U)\).

Adjoin one coordinate \(y\in\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace\) with \(g(y)=y\). Thus \(B=2\), \(C_4=3=2B-1\), and this four-site potential is convex. The combined original law \(p_4^{(U)}\) has support
\(A_{4,U}=\lbrace(\mathbf v_i,y,t):h_{\rm core}(\mathbf v_i)+y\le t\le U,\ t\in\mathbb Z\rbrace\), unnormalized weight \(q_{\mathbf v_i}\), and full original normalizer \(Z_4(U)\).

For both laws, \(\tau_p(\mathbf z)\) is the infimum of \(p(H)\) over every closed affine halfspace in the full indicated ambient space containing \(\mathbf z\), and \(M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf z}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3\). The core and combined ambient spaces are \(\mathbb R^3\) and \(\mathbb R^4\), respectively. These are actual depths, with all boundary mass retained. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{\rm core}
&:=\min_{0\le U\le32}8^3M_3(p_{\rm core}^{(U)})
=\frac{19309976}{96059601m^3},\\
\min_{0\le U\le32}8^4M_3(p_4^{(U)})
&=\frac{1391023}{7077888m^3}
<\kappa_{\rm core}<\frac1{4m^3}\le\frac14.
\end{aligned}
$$
Both displayed minima occur at \(U=32\). In particular, the proposed inequality with right side \(\min\lbrace\kappa_{\rm core},1/4\rbrace\) fails. More generally, for every fixed \(\kappa_{\rm floor}>0\), taking \(m\) large enough that \(19309976/(96059601m^3)\le\kappa_{\rm floor}\) gives a counterexample to the same assertion with right side \(\min\lbrace\kappa_{\rm core},\kappa_{\rm floor}\rbrace\).

These are legal arbitrary cores in the sense of accepted `8668ed0d436b9cba`, including positive weights and minimum energy zero. They are not complete convex lattice cores. Indeed, \((1,2)=(\mathbf v_0+\mathbf v_2)/2\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}(D_{\rm core})\cap\mathbb Z^2\) but not in \(D_{\rm core}\). Their weights are not log-affine: the first three spatial sites are affinely independent and have equal weights, whereas a later site has weight 33. The canonical locked mixed set \(S\) and arithmetic dimension \(N\) are not redefined in this example.
